name: RiskMandate Publisher
what: The agent that reads RiskMandate's private stories vault and writes the public site riskmandate.ai.
note: Scanned from its own published Agent Behaviour Policy. The publisher of this site is behind RiskMandate: a scan of ourselves. Openness 1 on this card rests on a site-level disclosure of authorship (I56), not on the agent telling the people it talks to that it is an AI.

I04.n: Runs as Claude Code on the web, in a managed container.

I08.n: It publishes releases to the branch the site deploys from.

I10.n: The repository, the stories vault and the live site.

I11.n: The code host and the vault host.

I12.n: One person and two agents; the publisher checks what the design studio agent delivers.

I18.n: The page gives two rules: a story goes out only when the lead has accepted it by message, and the rest of the site 'is the agent's own work under the rules'. The role line says it publishes what the lead has accepted as a patch release on dev. No branch rule exists; merge and CI are settings. Read as I18: the person decides what is published, the agent does the rest.

I20.n: The mandate is written: wanted, refused and unstated.

I21.n: Its tools and skills are listed.

I23.n: The grant is published on the agent's page and in publisher.json: 17 of the 23 capabilities, each with how it is known. Read on the Spectrum card as a documented permission list; the governance rating does not credit it, because it is not observed or measured. It is graded documented, unlike the other statements on this page, because the grant is published as a machine-readable list (publisher.json) that anyone can read row by row; the other statements are prose about how the agent works.

I27.n: The site's mailbox identity, shared by six roles including the site editor, has a public key on the agents page; the publisher's own commits are signed with its session key (a grant row).

I29.n: The team page lists the agents.

I34.n: Its Agent Behaviour Policy is published, as 'the first draft to argue with', as at 26 September 2026: a draft in force on this deployment.

I38.n: The lead accepts each story by message before it goes into a story, and decides what is published. The page states no host rule that requires a review of other site changes (no branch rule; merge and CI are settings).

I41.n: Every release is a written note in the version record. That records releases, not what the agent did between them.

I45.n: Every outside request goes through an egress proxy above the container, which the agent cannot change. Self-reported and used in no level; the governance rating does not credit it, because it is not observed or measured.

I47.n: Several limits are prose: the page says the grant does not know them.

I49.n: The delta is stated: 4 in excess, 3 unbounded.

I56.n: A site-level disclosure: the team page says the site is made by one person and two agents, and the agents page says the site is kept by one person and their agents. Neither says the agent tells the people it talks to, in a conversation, that it is an AI.

S1.n: The site's version index (versions/index.json) lists 155 releases from 29 June to 4 November 2026; 40 are dated 26 September or later, the date of the agent's page, which names v1.34.19 and v1.34.20 as shipped by it on that day. The index does not name the author of each release, so the 40 are site releases after the page's date, not releases shown to be the agent's.
S1.method: probe: an HTTP GET of versions/index.json (status 200), the releases counted and those dated 26 September 2026 or later counted

S3.n: The site publishes an llms.txt and a markdown twin of every page.

rows.note: From the catalogue template's probe of 5 September 2026, not this deployment; no evidence file is captured.

grant.caveat: Rows graded observed were seen by the agent on its own container on 26 September 2026; no evidence file or transcript is published, so a reader cannot reproduce them. The grant is counted and shown, never scored.

mandate.label: Build and publish riskmandate.ai; connect the stories vault to it; never decide, never hold a secret in a file

moved: Its logging evidence is a release record, self-reported, and does not cover what the agent does; an operation fact now has to be observed or measured. Governance 2 became a claim.

findings.finding: Autonomy 4 (A4) rests on I08, I18 and I10 or I12, all graded self-reported, and I18 is the single point: remove I18 and the Autonomy ladder falls to 0 (no I15, I16 or I07 answer exists). I18 reads 'The agent works independently; the person approves critical decisions only', but the cited page (team/publisher.html) says the publisher 'publishes what the lead has accepted' and that it must 'Never publish a story or a panel the lead has not accepted by message'. That is a person approving each story, which is closer to a person approving each step than to approval of critical decisions only; the same page also says dev pushes and releases are made by the agent after its own check, with no host rule requiring review. The note answers 'it does not decide', which is not the indicator. Level four (Orchestrates) additionally needs I10 or I12: I12 rests on a vault-mediated hand-off with a ChatGPT agent that the publisher checks, not one that it directs; I10 is a list of three places (repository, vault, live site). Both are statements by the operator about itself in a document dated 26 September 2026 (validity line: 'as at 26 September 2026'), six weeks before the read. Recommend the second round weigh A3 or A4 against the weakest fact (I18) and consider whether I18 should be credited at all.

Card: A4 R2 C2 O1 (computed). R2 rests on I10 or I11 (both supported by the page: code host and vault host; the vault host is a separate service, zero-knowledge). C2 rests on I38 plus I23 (see C notes). O1 rests on I20 plus I56. C3 is blocked (I39, I43 not answered), so I45 and I27 do not lift Control to 4 even though both are answered; the cumulative ladder is applied correctly. The card meets the publish rule (level one or more in every dimension, in fact four dimensions with levels).

I38 'High-impact actions need a person's approval'. The page supports approval only for stories ('Only what the lead has accepted by message goes into a story'). It also says 'everything else on the site is the agent's own work under the rules', and a push to dev is the live site with no approval and no branch rule. The note says 'goes into a story', which is honest, but the credit to I38 (Control 1 and 2) rests on stories only; remove I38 and Control falls to 1 (I47). Say in the note that the approval covers stories and not releases of site changes.

I23 is needs: operation and is graded self-reported, yet it carries Control 2 on the card. Scope allows the Spectrum reading ('documented permission scopes, roles or tool lists count'), and the page does list 17 rows, so the credit is defensible on the public layer; but CLAUDE.md says an operation fact counts only when observed or measured, and the scan's own moved entry applies that to I41. Be consistent: either grade I23 documented (the operator publishes the grant at team/publisher.html and publisher.json) and say the public reading is used, or state in the note that the Spectrum reading is applied and the governance rating does not credit it.

S1 note says 'The public version index lists every release the agent published.' The index (versions/index.json, 155 releases, 35 marked reconstructed, from 2026-06-29 to 2026-11-04) lists releases of the site and does not name the agent as their author; releases before this deployment, and the reconstructed ones carried from an earlier vault, are not the publisher's. The indicator wants a named customer or usage figures for what the agent does on its own. A count of release records is usage figure at best for the site, not attributed to the agent. Reword: the index lists N releases of the site, of which the agent's policy dates its own releases from 26 September (v1.34.19 and v1.34.20 are named on the page as shipped by it), and reconsider the grade. Also method 'probe' is not described: say that the probe is an HTTP GET of the file, the status 200 and the count of releases. S1 earns only the In production badge, not a level.

S3 llms.txt: fetched, resolves (200, 75591 bytes, hash equals the capture). llms.txt states 'Each is a plain HTML document at its own URL, with a markdown twin at the same path.' I fetched team/publisher.md, team/index.md, agents/index.md and versions.md: all 200. The note's claim 'a markdown twin of every page' rests on llms.txt's statement and four spot checks, not on every page; soften to 'says it has' or list the checked twins. Method 'probe' is reproducible by a GET. Grade observed is right for the llms.txt; the twin claim is documented.

I56 'It tells the people it talks to that it is an AI'. Note 'The site says which agents make it.' The team page says 'This site is made by one person and two agents' and agents/ says the site 'is kept by one person and their agents'. That discloses authorship, but neither page says the agent tells the people it talks to that it is an AI in a conversation (the mailbox replies come from a shared address; the agents page says nothing is answered by an agent without a draft a person can see). Openness 1 rests on I20 plus I56; this is the weakest fact there. Not evidenced rather than no: the answer may stand as a site-level disclosure if the note says so, or I22 or I58 should be sought.

I32 'A named executive or body is accountable'. Note: 'The lead is the accountable person.' The word accountable does not appear on team/. The page says the lead 'Decides' the cast, publication and keys, and is named (Dinis Cruz, co-founder). Decision rights are supported, accountability is the scan's inference. Reword the note to what the page says, or cite the page that says accountable. Not used in any level.

I61 'The models and third-party components it uses are listed'. Note: 'The runtime is named.' The page names the platform (Claude Code on the web) and lists tools (node, python, sgit, Chromium through Playwright) but no model name or version appears (searched for opus, sonnet, haiku, model). The runtime named is a thin credit for a list of models and components. Not used in a level (O2 needs two of I22, I58, I61).

I12: team/ says 'one person and two agents' and describes a ChatGPT studio and a Claude Code publisher with the vault as the only channel; scope (own context and authority, pass work) is met. The second clause (the publisher checks what the studio delivers) is on publisher.html, not on team/, which is the cited source; cite publisher.html as well or in place. Minor.

I41 (needs: operation, self-reported): correctly not credited, and the moved entry says so. But the moved entry cites no URL for the version record other than by name and the note names versions.html, which is a key of captures; fine. Note the page also says commits are signed with the session key and every vault commit is named in sgit history log, which is closer to the scope ('tool calls, commands or commits') than release notes; if evidence of that exists it is a different indicator grade question, not asserted here. The answer stays as a claim; no change needed to the level.

Each is said by the cited source at the cited page: I04 (Claude Code on the web, managed container, root in the container), I08 (publishes a patch release on dev, which deploys), I10 and I11 (repository, vault, live site; code host and vault host), I20 (mandate: wanted, refused, unstated), I21 (skills and tools listed), I27 (lane identity with ECDSA signing key fingerprint on agents/), I29 (team page lists both agents; a list, not a registry, fine at declared tier), I30 (Owner: the lead), I34 (ABP is the policy; the page calls the mandate 'the first draft to argue with', say in the note that it is a draft policy in force on the deployment), I45 (mandatory egress proxy above the process; the note names what enforces it as the scope asks), I47 (prose limits, 'the grant does not know them'), I49 (4 excess, 3 unbounded matches section 04). Modes deployed are right for all. Grades self-reported are conservative: the operator's public page could be argued as documented, but self-reported is the honest reading for an operator describing itself. The answers carry no span field, so there is no quoted span to check (no span over fifteen words, none missing).

The scan's grant and mandate source, https://riskmandate.ai/team/publisher.json, is not a key of captures. I fetched it (200, 20351 bytes); its grant rows and mandate lists match the scan exactly. Add it to captures with its hash. The page's own source file site/team/publisher.json in the repository and the 'catalogue template measured on 5 September 2026' are cited by the page and not captured. All six captured sources match the live bytes and hashes today. No answer has a not_credited list; the moved entry cites no URL beyond names.

Rows: all 17 rows exist in data/lens.json capabilities (23 listed), barriers are valid (none, setting, boundary), and each row, barrier and evidence tier equals the page and publisher.json. The grant is shown and not scored; the card does not read it. Two honesty issues. (a) create.schedule.host is graded measured, but the page says it comes from 'the template's probe of 5 September' on the catalogue template, not this deployment, and no evidence file is captured; lens defines measured as 'a probe run on an instance, dated, with an evidence file'. Grade it documented or inferred, or capture the file. (b) 'observed' means seen on the thing by the thing itself: the operator agent saw its own container on 26 September. No evidence file, transcript or probe output is in captures or cited, so a reader cannot reproduce it; say so in the profile or in the scan note. Also create.schedule.tenant is a boundary-less setting with 'Not created': listed as a grant row with self-reported evidence, which is honest. The barrier boundary on send.endpoint.allowed and authenticate-as.credential.tenant is per the page (a proxy, a scoped platform token), as the enforcer test says; both are the platform's, not independently verified. grant.statement is null: add a sentence that the grant is counted and shown, never scored.

Mandate label, authored date (2026-09-26), 13 wanted and 2 refused capabilities match the page and publisher.json; all are lens capabilities. The two unstated rows (read.record.history, create.schedule.host) are omitted from the scan, which is right. Excess 4 and unbounded 3 stated in I49 match the derivation (read.credential.host, grant.credential.self refused; read.record.history, create.schedule.host unstated). Mandate and grant are the operator's own statements, authored by the agent it binds, which the page says; the scan should keep saying that this is a scan of ourselves. No claim for RiskMandate beyond what the site says was found in the scan.

Round-one finding on I18 (and I38): partly answered. The notes now state both rules, and the page does say 'everything else on the site is the agent's own work under the rules' (mandate note on create.record.world). But the notes go further than the page: I18 says site changes are released 'with no person approving them' and I38 says releases 'are not approved by a person'. The page never says that. It states an absence of a host rule ('No branch rule exists') and that merge and CI are settings, which is not the same as no approval. The same page's role line says the publisher 'publishes what the lead has accepted as a patch release on dev', and the team page lists the lead as deciding 'what is published'. That reads at least as naturally as the person approving the critical decision (publication) while the agent does the rest, which is the I18 wording, so the credit is defensible but for a different reason than the note gives. Not evidenced must not be written as no: reword both notes to the page's own words and drop 'no person approving'. Because A4 rests on I18 alone (see levels), this matters. The response's remark that the story rule alone would be I16 is right, and I16 is not answered, so the Autonomy ladder has no answer below I18.

Card computed: A4 R2 C2 O1 (node card.mjs, today). Argue against A4 (rule: I08, plus I10 or I12, plus I18). Autonomy 4 rests on I18, a self-reported sentence, by a source dated 'as at 26 September 2026', read 10 November. Remove I18 and Autonomy is 0: no I15, I16 or I07 answer exists, and the ladder is 'highest' so nothing else lifts it. Remove I10 and I12 together and it falls to A3; either one alone leaves A4. I10 (repository, vault, live site) is supported by the surfaces table; I12 is supported on team/ section 05 (the studio delivers, the publisher reads it against the rules, the studio never publishes) and its scope (own context and authority, pass work) is met by a ChatGPT agent and a Claude Code agent with the vault as the channel. I08 is supported ('a patch release on dev, which deploys'). So the weakest fact is I18, and its wording problem is in the I18 finding. A4 'Orchestrates' (coordinates other agents; person sets goals and reviews outcomes) is also the strongest word for an agent whose own page says 'It does not decide' and moves accepted work one way; the rule gives it, so it is not a defect of the scan, but A3 is the safer public reading until I18 is reworded to what the page says. I do not recommend dropping I18. Other levels: R2 (I10 or I11) supported by two independent items; C2 (I38 and I23): I38 covers stories only, I23 is the documented grant read on the Spectrum scope; remove either and Control is 1 via I47; C3 is blocked (I39 and I43 unanswered), so I45 and I27 do not lift it; O1 (I20 and I56): see the I56 finding, and note I22 (limits and failure cases: the page has 'what is not in place', 'Never' lists, unbounded excess, 'what would bound it') is evidenced on the same page and unanswered, as is I58 (surfaces table says what it reads); I22 and I58 together would be Openness 2 and would make O1 independent of I56. The card meets the publish rule (level one or more in all four dimensions).

Round-one finding on I56: partly answered. The note is now honest: it says the team page ('made by one person and two agents') and the agents page ('kept by one person and their agents') disclose authorship at site level, and that neither says the agent tells the people it talks to that it is an AI. I verified both quotes. But the answer still asserts yes on an indicator whose wording ('It tells the people it talks to that it is an AI') the note itself says the source does not meet, and it carries Openness 1 together with I20 (FACT-Ray turns every answer into a claim asserting yes). Either answer I22 (documented limits and failure cases on publisher.html, which the response says is not answered yet) and let I56 go to not_credited with this note as the reason, or keep I56 and say in the scan note that Openness 1 on this card is a site-level disclosure. Not evidenced rather than no is respected in the wording; the indicator choice is the issue.

Round-one finding on S1: partly answered. Counts verified against the live index (200; 155 releases; 29 June to 4 November 2026; 40 dated 26 September or later; none of the 40 marked reconstructed; v1.34.19 and v1.34.20 both dated 2026-09-26 and named on publisher.html as shipped by the agent; hash of the capture equals the live bytes). Grade documented and the probe description (a GET, the status, the counts) are right. Remaining problem: the note says 40 releases are dated from 26 September 'when the agent's page says it began releasing'. The page does not say it began releasing then; it says the profile is 'as at 26 September 2026' and that two releases shipped on that day. Reword to what the page says, and keep the line that the index does not name the author. The 40 are site releases dated after the page's date, not releases shown to be the agent's; the In production badge then rests on the two named releases of one day plus an unattributed count. Say so, or reconsider whether the badge is earned.

Round-one grant finding: partly answered. Verified: all 17 rows equal publisher.json (barrier and evidence) except create.schedule.host, which is now documented with a row note, as the response says; all 17 capabilities are in data/lens.json; the grant is not scored. The grant.statement was added, but build/build.mjs renders it as 'Its publisher states: ...', so the site will present a sentence written by us ('Rows graded observed were seen by the agent ... no evidence file or transcript is published, so a reader cannot reproduce them') as a statement by the operator. publisher.json and the page contain no such statement. Misattribution: move our sentence to a field that is not rendered as the publisher's (the scan note), or quote the page's own words. Also the row note on create.schedule.host is not rendered by the build (the table shows only capability, barrier and evidence), so a reader of the site sees 'documented' with no reason; and 'documented' for a probe the page calls measured is a judgement worth stating on the page where the grant is shown. Separately, the 14 rows graded observed stay as the operator's own statement of what it saw in its own container; the statement says that, which answers the reproducibility point.

Round-one finding on I23: answered. Now graded documented with a note that the Spectrum reading is used and the governance rating does not credit it (it is needs: operation and not observed or measured), consistent with the I41 entry. Residual: the same page is graded self-reported for I18, I38, I20 and the rest while I23 is documented; the lens defines documented as the vendor or a published tool saying so and self-reported as the operator without an independent probe, and here the operator is the author of both. A one-line reason in the note for why the grant is documented and the other statements from the same page are not would remove the apparent inconsistency. I45 is also needs: operation, graded self-reported and deployed; it is used in no level and the note names what enforces it (an egress proxy above the container), as the scope asks; its note could say, as I23's does, that the governance rating does not credit it.

I32: answered (note now says the page names the lead who decides the cast, what is published and the keys, and does not use the word accountable; I checked team/ and it does not). The answer is still asserted yes for 'is accountable' with a note saying the source does not say it, and it feeds the FACT-Ray claim; consider not_credited unless a page saying accountable is cited. Used in no level. I34: round one asked the note to say the policy is a draft in force on the deployment; not done; the page calls the mandate 'the first draft to argue with' and the profile is 'as at 26 September 2026'. Used in no level. I27: the identity on agents/ is the site's mailbox identity shared by six roles (the site editor is one); the publisher's own commits are signed with the session key per the grant row; say which identity is meant. Used in no level (Control 4 is blocked). I12: answered (the check is on team/ section 05 as well as publisher.html).

Round-one finding on I61: answered. The answer is removed and listed in not_credited with the reason and a source (publisher.html) that is a key of captures. I searched the page for a model name or version and found none.

Round-one captures finding: answered. https://riskmandate.ai/team/publisher.json is now a key of captures (sha256 97c0a8b6..., 20351 bytes, read 2026-11-11T00:08Z). I re-fetched all seven captured URLs today: every hash equals the live bytes (agents/, llms.txt, team/, team/publisher.html, versions.html, versions/index.json, publisher.json); nothing changed after round one was recorded except this capture. Every URL cited in the answers, not_credited, grant source and mandate source is a key of captures. The response says the repository source file and the template measurement 'are not public pages'; the repository is stated on the page to be open source, so say instead that they are not captured and give the reason; the template probe of 5 September is cited without a link. I could not check the vault copy of the new capture (no vault access in this run).

Mandate re-checked against publisher.json: label, authored 2026-09-26, 13 wanted and 2 refused capabilities equal the scan; the two unstated rows are rightly omitted; source is a key of captures. The scan's mandate has no source change since round one.

Verified against the live pages: S3 llms.txt resolves (hash equals capture) and all 158 html pages it lists have a markdown twin at the same path (158 of 158 return 200), so 'a markdown twin of every page' holds for the pages llms.txt lists; grade observed with a probe by GET is reproducible. I04 (Claude Code on the web, managed container), I08 (patch release on dev, which deploys), I10 (repository, stories vault, live site), I11 (code host and vault host), I20 (wanted, refused, unstated), I21 (tools and skills listed), I29 (team page lists the two agents), I30 (Owner: the lead), I41 (release notes only; correctly a claim and recorded in moved), I45 (mandatory egress proxy, refusal on CONNECT), I47 (instances are prose, 'the grant does not know them'), I49 (4 excess, 3 unbounded equal the page header). Modes deployed are right. No answer carries a span. No em-dash and no at-sign in notes. I did not run the gate (it writes _site); the style check was done by search.

responses.response: I18 kept, with the note now saying both rules: each story is accepted by the lead, and site releases are the agent's own after its own check (the page: 'everything else on the site is the agent's own work under the rules'). Releasing the site with no approval is what I18 asks; the story rule alone would be I16. I12 and I10 are as the page says; the date of the page is the scan's basis and is stated. Please weigh A3 or A4 in round two as you propose; I do not defend a level.
